description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: C.J. Stroud connected on 26-of-38 passes for 274 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.impact: Stroud added 15 yards on a couple of carries and did not throw an interception in Sunday's season opener. He did lose a couple of fumbles, however, as the Texans took a loss in this Week 1 shootout. Still, this was an encouraging start for the third-year QB, and he's certainly at least going to be on the streaming radar for a Week 2 matchup with the Bengals.
items.title: C.J. Stroud plays well in Week 1 loss

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Woody Marks rushed for 42 yards on nine carries and caught his only target for a two-yard loss in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.impact: Marks was certainly involved in the offense behind new workhorse back David Montgomery on Sunday. Marks averaged close to 5.0 yards per carry on his nine attempts. He'll remain a useful handcuff to Montgomery for now.
items.title: Woody Marks gets 10 touches in Week 1

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: The Buffalo Bills D/ST had two fumble recoveries and three sacks against the Texans on Sunday in their 36-31 win.
items.impact: Buffalo had a "bend, don't break" sort of game against Houston, especially in the final minutes. The Texans had worked their way down the field to try for a potential game winning touchdown, but a strip sack on Houston QB CJ Stroud sealed the deal for the Bills. Overall their performance was fine given the turnovers they forced, but not spectacular given the points given up. They'll face the Lions high powered offense on Thursday.
items.title: Buffalo Bills D/ST comes up big in win over Houston

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Tyler Bass hit all three of his PATs and all three of his field goal attempts on his way to 12 kicking points in the Bills' 36-31 win over Houston.
items.impact: Bass had himself a great week against the Texans defense, spurred by the amount of offense Josh Allen and the rest of the crew were getting. He should be a good value moving forward as part of this high-powered offense.
items.title: Tyler Bass has big week in win over Houston

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Titans signed LB Jimmy Ciarlo to their practice squad.
items.impact: Ciarlo was previously with the Bills. He'll add depth in the linebacker room for Tennessee.
items.title: Jimmy Ciarlo signs with Titans

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: David Montgomery rushed for 60 yards and two scores on 20 carries, adding three receptions for 19 yards and another touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.impact: Montgomery was given 23 touches in his debut with the Texans, as the veteran back was a focal point of the offense. Granted, he only averaged 3.0 yards per carry, but he found the end zone three times while being involved both on the ground and through the air.
items.title: David Montgomery has big debut for Texans

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Dawson Knox caught just one pass for seven yards in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans.
items.impact: Knox is playing second fiddle to Dalton Kincaid in the tight end pecking order, and even further down in the overall order. He's not worth starting unless Kincaid misses time, and even then could be a bit iffy.
items.title: Dawson Knox uninvolved in win over Texans

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Ray Davis had a single carry for three yards in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also returned two kicks for 51 yards.
items.impact: Davis is operating as the RB2 behind James Cook and one of the Bills primary special teams returners, which is a good sign of trust. While he didn't see much of anything on offense this week, should anything happen to Cook, Davis will be a high priority pickup.
items.title: Ray Davis sees single carry in win

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Nico Collins grabbed 7-of-10 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.impact: Nico Collins played his typical go-to role for QB C.J. Stroud on Sunday. Collins led the team in receptions, targets, and yards. He also found the end zone for the first time this season, hitting paydirt on a 12-yard play just before halftime. Collins is a WR1 for fantasy purposes.
items.title: Nico Collins turns in strong season debut

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Joshua Palmer caught one of two targets for 34 yards and a score in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.impact: Palmer's fantasy day was saved by the touchdown, but unless you have him in bestball formats, it didn't do your team much good. He's the fifth best target at best in Buffalo right now, so it will be slim pickings with the roster currently healthy.
items.title: Joshua Palmer snags touchdown in win over Houston

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Kayshon Boutte caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.impact: Boutte was acquired from New England late in the preseason to shore up the Texans' wide receiver corps. His big-play potential is known from the last couple of years with the Patriots, but his targets were predictably limited in an offense that is still relatively new to him. Boutte is a wait-and-see bench stash in standard fantasy leagues.
items.title: Kayshon Boutte makes only catch in Texans debut

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Keon Coleman caught his only target for a yard in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.impact: Coleman was very quiet in a game where Josh Allen threw for over 300 yards. He's off of fantasy radars right now, and will need to show some signs of life before being brought back into fantasy lineups.
items.title: Keon Coleman quiet in big win over Houston

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Jaylin Noel hauled in both of his targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.impact: Noel only got two looks from C.J. Stroud on Sunday, but he had the longest gain of the day with a 35-yard pickup. The second-year receiver out of Iowa State has big-play potential every week, but he may not see enough volume to move beyond being a boom-or-bust fantasy option.
items.title: Jaylin Noel shows big-play ability on limited targets

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Khalil Shakir caught four of six targets for 50 yards in the Bills' 36-31 win over Houston on Sunday.
items.impact: Shakir operated as Josh Allen's safety valve underneath with DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid working over the top. That's been Shakir's role in the past, so don't expect it to stop any time soon. His upside is capped because of it, but he's a decent flex play in PPR formats if you need a solid floor.
items.title: Khalil Shakir goes for 50 yards in win

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.impact: Hutchinson saw the third-most targets from C.J. Stroud on Sunday. The Texans are looking for a No. 2 wide receiver to emerge behind Nico Collins, and though Hutchinson's upside may be limited, he might be the guy at the moment. The fourth-year pro hauled in 35 passes for 428 yards and three scores over 17 games last season.
items.title: Xavier Hutchinson finishes with three grabs in Week 1

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Dalton Schultz secured 4-of-8 targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.impact: Schultz caught a career-high 82 passes last season, and he remains a steady presence in the Texans' offense. The veteran tight end finished second on the team with eight targets, trailing only Nico Collins' 10. Schultz has a limited ceiling, but he's almost always on the TE streaming radar.
items.title: Dalton Schultz hauls in four passes

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: DJ Moore caught 5 of 8 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans.
items.impact: Moore looked good and re-invigorated in this game, showing off some of his old self against a Houston defense that didn't look like its normal self. His touchdown was a bit fluky, as the defensive back solely made a play on the ball and failed do to so, leaving no one around Moore while he walked in for a score. But, fantasy managers won't be complaining. Next up for DJ are the Detroit Lions, who just allowed big days for Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele on Sunday.
items.title: DJ Moore goes for 100 yards in win over Houston

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Dalton Kincaid caught five of six targets for 130 yards in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.impact: Kincaid had arguably his best game as a pro, acheiving a career-high 130 receiving yards in what should have been tough sledding against Houston. He tied with Khalil Shakir for second in targets on the Bills, but vastly outproduced Shakir in yards. His downfield usage was encouraging, and it's a promising start to his fourth season. Now to see if it keeps up.
items.title: Dalton Kincaid has breakout game against Texans

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Ka'imi Fairbairn made his only field-goal try and all four of his PATs in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.impact: Fairbairn showed off his powerful leg in Sunday's loss, nailing a 58-yard attempt to briefly give the Texans a one-point lead in the fourth quarter. The veteran has been kicking for the Texans since 2017 and remains one of the more reliable options in the league.
items.title: Ka'imi Fairbairn puts seven points on the board

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: James Cook III ran 13 times for 57 yards and caught three of four targets for 12 yards in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.impact: Cook was fine on his touches and was saved by his three receptions in PPR formats, but it fantasy managers will be hoping for more. He's still a premium running back, and he will get his chance early this week as the Bills play the Lions on Thursday night.
items.title: James Cook III goes for 69 yards in big win over Texans

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: The Texans D/ST allowed 36 points on 409 yards of total offense while coming up with two sacks and no takeaways in Sunday's loss to the Bills.
items.impact: The Texans should feature a solid defensive unit this season, but they ran into a potent Bills' offense in Week 1. Powered by QB Josh Allen, the Bills shredded the Texans' pass defense, totaling 334 yards and a couple of scores through the air. Houston did come up with a couple of sacks, but Allen mostly had his way. The Texans will face another top-tier QB when Joe Burrow and the Bengals visit Houston in Week 2.
items.title: Texans defense struggles to contain Bills in Week 1

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Josh Allen completed 20-of-29 passes for 334 yards with two touchdowns with an additional 23 yards and two scores on the ground on six carries in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.impact: Allen was in complete control on Sunday, carving up what should have been a difficult Texans defense on his way to a four touchdown performance. He will have another nice matchup against Detroit on Thursday who just allowed a 30-point game to the Saints.
items.title: Josh Allen dismantles Houston defense in big win

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: The San Fransisco 49ers D/ST shut down the Rams offense on Thursday, allowing just seven points in their 27-7 rout of the Super Bowl favorites.
items.impact: The Niners defensive totals were modest, with one interception and a fumble recovery, but were held without a sack. They just kept the Rams from moving the ball while not racking up much in the "counting stats" category. It's a good showing for the team, and a date with the Dolphins is on tap. They are a great DST option this week if available.
items.title: San Fransisco 49ers D/ST shuts down Rams in win

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Commanders DE Dorance Armstrong has officially been reinstated by the league following his Week 1 suspension.
items.impact: Armstrong will be back for Week 2 against the Cowboys.
items.title: Dorance Armstrong Jr. reinstated from suspension

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said T.J. Tampa could miss some time.
items.impact: The team is still gathering more information on a knee injury for Tampa.
items.title: T.J. Tampa Jr. (knee) to miss some time
